rows.answer:
The build was broken due to two compiler errors in src/ring_buffer.cpp:
1. Line 13: 'count' was not declared in this scope (should be 'count_')
2. Line 27: expected ';' before '}' token (missing semicolon)

I fixed both issues by:
1. Changing `++count;` to `++count_;` to match the member variable name declared in the header
2. Adding a semicolon to `bool RingBuffer::empty() const { return count_ == 0 }` to make it `bool RingBuffer::empty() const { return count_ == 0; }`

The build now succeeds and all tests pass.

history.name: propose_patch

arguments.find: bool RingBuffer::full() const { return count_ + 1 == slots_.size(); }
arguments.replace: bool RingBuffer::full() const { return count_ == slots_.size(); }
arguments.rationale: The bug is in the full() method logic. When a ring buffer has capacity N, it should be considered full when it contains exactly N elements. The current implementation incorrectly returns true when count_ = N-1, which means it thinks the buffer is full when it still has space for one more element. This causes the push operation to fail incorrectly on what should be the third push in a 3-element buffer.

The bug was in src/ring_buffer.cpp line 29 where the condition was `count_ + 1 == slots_.size()` instead of `count_ == slots_.size()`. This caused the buffer to be incorrectly marked as full when it still had space for one more element, preventing the third push operation from succeeding. I fixed this by changing the condition to correctly check if the count equals the slot size, which properly indicates when the buffer is full. The test now passes.
